text:
marta: heads-up — i'm kicking off a small sweep of deepbench vs the new "quantized-ggml" intake. want to align on what the 'compatibility sentinel' should treat as a hard fail vs an alert. i ran a quick smoke and saw tokenization variance on a couple prompts.
jen: quick q — are we treating tokenizer diffs as a compatibility failure or just a noisy alert?
raj: my vote: tokenization diffs alone = alert (soft). generation divergences on the golden inputs = hard fail. tokenization can be platform / pip dependent.
sam: agreed with raj. but we need concrete thresholds. otherwise everyone interprets "divergence" differently.
marta: ok. proposal:
- prefilter at intake: cheap tokenization check (cpu) to catch obvious mismatches early. if token count delta > 10% mark as "prefilter-fail" and route to deeper bench.
- sentinel alert when top-1 tokenization mismatch on >3% of golden set.
- sentinel hard fail when generation metric delta (avg rouge/bleu/perplexity as defined in onboarding) exceeds 5% on our golden 512 sample.
jen: can we make the prefilter a tiny delta check instead of full tokenization? e.g. hash of first 64 bytes tokenized length? cheaper to run in the intake path.
raj: yeah, implement as: call tokenizer.encode(input[:512]) and compare len and a 32-bit fingerprint of the token ids. quick and portable. if mismatch, enqueue for deepbench.
jen: example prefilter snippet i sketched:```python
# intake prefilter
ids = tokenizer.encode(text[:512])
fingerprint = zlib.crc32(bytes(ids[:64]))
if abs(len(ids)-gold_len) > gold_len*0.1 or fingerprint != gold_fp:
    mark_prefilter_flag()
```
sam: for the sentinel thresholds i mentioned earlier: alert @ 2% perplexity delta, warn @ 5% generation token F1 drop, hard fail @ 7% perplexity or model crash rate > 0.5%. also add an "operator override" label for infra regressions.
marta: noted. another tradeoff: running deepbench for every intake slows throughput. so we should stratify: cheap prefilter -> mid-tier mini-bench (50 samples) -> full deepbench (512) only for flagged candidates.
raj: agree. also, we should separate 'compatibility' signals from 'performance' signals. e.g., a 10% latency increase shouldn't block admission unless it breaks customer SLOs. keep admission focused on correctness/semantics.
build-bot: CI result: `deepbench/sample-512` for quantized-ggml completed — pass rate 0.97, avg perplexity delta 1.9% (compared to golden). See: https://ci.internal/deepbench/4325
jen: nice. can we wire that CI link into the sentinel's evaluation trace so reviewers can click through? add to admit UI.
sam: action items: (1) raj -> prototype prefilter (cpu) and push PR to intake by EOD, (2) sam -> add sentinel threshold config to admit schema + default values, (3) jen -> update onboarding doc with tokenization-as-soft-fail rationale and mini-bench flow, (4) marta -> schedule 15m review tomorrow to validate prototype results.
marta: small UX note — when sentinel flags a model, include short reproducible command that runs the exact mini-bench locally (curl + docker cmd). avoids back-and-forth.
jen: i'll add the `--repro` curl snippet to the admit UI.
raj: one more gotcha — quantized runtimes sometimes reorder sub-byte packing; make sure our token fingerprinting ignores endianness and minor packing differences. use token ids rather than raw bytes.
marta: good catch. ok team, thanks — :thumbsup: i'll post the 15m invite. if anyone hits blockers with prototype, ping me in thread.
sam: :thumbsup:
build-bot: prometheus alert: inbound-deepbench-queue length spiked to 180 at 1734500200 (auto-scaled).
